newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - April 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - April 22.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian golfer Karrie Webb claimed her fifth career victory in a win in the US$US500,000 ($A650,000) Komen International championship on Sunday. The 22-year-old defeated Americans Nanci Bowen, Lorie Kane and Maggie Johnston-Forbes by two strokes to take out the event. Page 19.

Australian soccer coach Terry Venables has convinced Soccer Australia to drop the controversial Travellers versus True Blues series and to replace it with a Possibles-Probables format. The contenders series - to be played in Melbourne on May 28 and Sydneyon June 4 - will feature teams mixed with expatriate stars and Australian-based players. Page 18. --

The stomping allegations against New South Wales rugby union player Michael Brial were last night thrown out by a judiciary panel, only hours after ARU chief executive officer John O'Neill claimed Saturday's interstate clash was an embarrassment to the game. The panel found video evidence inconclusive. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian soccer player Aurelio Vidmar has set himself one last major career goal - to captain Australia to the 1998 World Cup finals. The 30-year-old striker is out of favour with his Spanish club, Tenerife, but is in demand from Australia after captainng the Socceroos to two recent victories in Europe. Page 44.

New Super League player Craig Gower last night ended Brisbane's unbeaten stretch in Super League with a dramatic field goal three minutes from full-time at Penrith Stadium to see Penrith defeat Brisbane 27-26. The 18-year-old kicked the one-pointer in front of a record crowd of 12,648. Page 46.

Australian Country Rugby League general manager David Barnhill claimed last night Super League was "cutting their own throat" by its moves to schedule Friday's Anzac Day Test at the same time as the annual Australian Rugby League Sydney-Country clash. Pag 46.
THE AGE

Australian swimmer Grant Hackett yesterday won the 1500 metres freestyle at the world short-course championships in Sweden. The 16-year-old took out the gold medal in the absence of word-record holder Kieren Perkins and Olympic silver medallist Daniel Kowlski by shaving 18 seconds off his personal best to win in 14 minutes 39.54 seconds. Page B8.

Australian golfer Greg Norman has lost his ranking as world number one player to American Tom Lehman after the release yesterday of the official world golf rankings. Norman has claimed the spot since June 1995 for a record 96 weeks on the back of his consistency on the US tour. Page B8.

The racial abuse of Australian Football League Melbourne player Jeff Farmer on Friday - for the second time in four weeks - will see the AFL toughen its racism policy. The League currently handles incidents of racial abuse through private mediation, but is believed to be considering an option that would publicly name offenders immediately. Page B8.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian Football League Essendon player Steve Alessio was last night suspended for three matches by the AFL Tribunal. Essendon has already been hit by injuries to key players, and may now have to find a temporary ruckman for Friday's match against Colingwood. Page 68.

Australian Football League Port Adelaide coach John Cahill goes against the conventional wisdom of most AFL coaches believing that the tradition of a "few quiet beers" after each match is crucial to his success in the sport. Cahill attributes his side's erly success in the AFL to the application of the 127-year-old club's tried and tested methods. Page 68.

Australian racehorses and Group 1 winners Poetic King and Count Chivas - who months ago were close to death - have been cleared to continue their careers with Poetic Justice set to return in Brisbane on Saturday and the results of Count Chivas' recent X-rys on a leg injury looking promising. Page 66.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The Queensland State Schools Rugby League Judiciary last night suspended two high school rugby league players for a year and banned 10 others for their roles in last Wednesday's Commonwealth Bank Cup Clairvaux-McKillop College match. A dozen players pleadd guilty for their role in the brawl. Page 68.

Confirmation of the New South Wales Government's plan to privatise the State TAB and introduce significant wagering taxation reforms will see punters emerging as the big winners. The State TAB will be linked to a lucrative statewide poker machine jackpot cheme. Page 62.

Australian racehorse Octagonal's reputation has spread far and wide with leading international studs negotiating to stand the recently retired racing champion at stud next year. Owners Jack and Bob Ingram have had inquiries from studs in America, Japan and Europe. Page 62.
